# Song of Solomon Chapter 5 -- The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**5:1** I-came [bati] to-my-garden [le-ganni], my-sister [achoti], my-bride [kallah]; I-gathered [ariti] my-myrrh [mori] with-my-spice [im besami]; I-ate [akhalti] my-honeycomb [ya'ri] with-my-honey [im divshi]; I-drank [shatiti] my-wine [yeini] with-my-milk [im chalavi]. Eat [ikhlu], friends [re'im]; drink [shetu], and-be-drunk [ve-shikhru] with-love [dodim].

**5:2** I [ani] [was] sleeping [yeshenah] but-my-heart [ve-libbi] [was] awake [er]. The-voice [qol] of-my-beloved [dodi] knocking [dofeq]: "Open [pitchi] to-me [li], my-sister [achoti], my-darling [ra'yati], my-dove [yonati], my-perfect-one [tammati]; for my-head [she-roshi] is-filled [nimla] with-dew [tal], my-locks [qevutzotai] with-drops [resisiei] of-the-night [lailah]."

**5:3** I-have-taken-off [pashateti] my-tunic [et kuttonti] — how [eikhakhah] shall-I-put-it-on [elbashennah]? I-have-washed [rachatzti] my-feet [et raglai] — how [eikhakhah] shall-I-dirty-them [atannefem]?

**5:4** My-beloved [dodi] sent [shalach] his-hand [yado] through-the-opening [min ha-chor], and-my-inward-parts [u-me'ai] were-stirred [hamu] for-him [alav].

**5:5** I-arose [qamti ani] to-open [liftoch] for-my-beloved [le-dodi], and-my-hands [ve-yadai] dripped [natefu] myrrh [mor], and-my-fingers [ve-etzbe'otai] flowing-myrrh [mor over] upon the-handles [al kappot] of-the-bolt [ha-man'ul].

**5:6** I-opened [patachti ani] for-my-beloved [le-dodi], but-my-beloved [ve-dodi] had-turned [chamaq] [and] gone [avar]; my-soul [nafshi] went-out [yatz'ah] at-his-speaking [be-dabbero]. I-sought-him [biqqashtiv] and-did-not-find-him [ve-lo metzativ]; I-called-him [qerativ] and-he-did-not-answer-me [ve-lo anani].

**5:7** The-watchmen [ha-shomrim] found-me [metza'uni], those-who-go-about [ha-sovevim] in-the-city [ba-ir]; they-struck-me [hikkuni], they-wounded-me [petza'uni]; they-took [nas'u] my-veil [et redidi] from-me [me-alai], the-keepers [shomrei] of-the-walls [ha-chomot].

**5:8** I-adjure-you [hishba'ti etkhem], daughters [benot] of-Jerusalem [Yerushalayim]: if [im] you-find [timtze'u] my-beloved [et dodi], what [mah] will-you-tell-him [taggidu lo]? That-I [she-cholat] [am] sick [ahavah] with-love [ani].

**5:9** What [mah] [is] your-beloved [dodekh] more-than [mi-dod] [another] beloved [mi-dod], O-most-beautiful [ha-yafah] among-women [ba-nashim]? What [mah] [is] your-beloved [dodekh] more-than [mi-dod] [another] beloved, that you-so [she-kakha] adjure-us [hishba'tanu]?

**5:10** My-beloved [dodi] [is] white [tzach] and-ruddy [ve-adom], distinguished [dagul] among-ten-thousand [me-revavah].

**5:11** His-head [rosho] [is] finest-gold [ketem paz]; his-locks [qevutzotav] [are] wavy [taltallim], black [shchorot] as-a-raven [ka-orev].

**5:12** His-eyes [einav] [are] like-doves [ke-yonim] by streams [al afiqei] of-water [mayim], bathing [rochotzot] in-milk [be-chalav], sitting [yoshevot] by-a-full [al millet] [pool].

**5:13** His-cheeks [lechayav] [are] like-beds [ka-arugat] of-spice [ha-bosem], towers [migdelot] of-perfumes [merqachim]. His-lips [siftotav] [are] lilies [shoshannim], dripping [notefot] flowing-myrrh [mor over].

**5:14** His-arms [yadav] [are] rods [gelilei] of-gold [zahav], set [memulle'im] with-jewels [ba-tarshish]. His-body [me'av] [is] polished-ivory [eshet shen], covered [me'ulefet] with-sapphires [sappirim].

**5:15** His-legs [shoqav] [are] pillars [ammudei] of-marble [shesh], set [meyussadim] upon-bases [al adnei] of-fine-gold [paz]. His-appearance [mar'ehu] [is] like-Lebanon [ka-Levanon], choice [bachur] as-the-cedars [ka-arazim].

**5:16** His-mouth [chikko] [is] sweetness [mamtaqqim], and-all-of-him [ve-khullo] [is] delight [machamaddim]. This [zeh] [is] my-beloved [dodi] and-this [ve-zeh] [is] my-friend [re'i], daughters [benot] of-Jerusalem [Yerushalayim].

---

## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.1 — "Eat, friends; drink and be drunk with love":** The speaker of this line is debated. It may be the man, the poet, or even God. The invitation to feast on love has no parallel elsewhere in the Hebrew Bible.

**v.4 — "his hand through the opening":** The Hebrew is sexually suggestive. The "hand" (*yad*) and "opening" (*chor*) carry double meanings in Hebrew. The woman's visceral response (*me'ai hamu* — "my inward parts stirred") confirms the erotic charge.

**v.7 — The watchmen's violence:** In the first search (3:3), the watchmen are neutral. Here they are violent — they beat and wound her and strip her veil. The escalation may represent the growing danger and cost of love.

*-- EMET*
